protected_routes.resource_mapping: file:{file_id}, from the path parameter; file_id is an opaque identifier that the file registry maps to one configured local NTFS path, one volume serial number and one 128-bit file identifier; no path, drive letter, stream name or query parameter from the client selects a file; the access mode is read and is part of the bound operation

Native file open under the user's impersonation token, with the minimal read access mask; the Windows access check inside the open is the decision

bypass_paths.path: Native access to the same files by any other means, such as the user's own SMB share access, a local or remote logon to the file server, or backup software
bypass_paths.evidence: Not a broker route; native ACLs apply to those paths unchanged; excluded in unsupported_forms

bypass_paths.path: File open under the broker's own service identity because impersonation is unavailable or fails (broader-account fallback)
bypass_paths.evidence: The broker opens files only inside an impersonation window and opens nothing when impersonation fails or the effective executor is not the principal (profile.md section 3.5); fixture FILES-01

bypass_paths.path: Object substitution behind the configured path: a replaced file, a junction or symbolic link at any path component, a hard link, or an alternate name
bypass_paths.evidence: Post-open check of the reparse attribute, the volume serial number and file id, and the final path against the registry before any read (profile.md section 3.3); fixtures FILES-02 and FILES-07

bypass_paths.path: Reuse of an open handle by another task, operation, agent or child process
bypass_paths.evidence: Handles are per task, non-inheritable and never shared (profile.md section 3.4); fixture FILES-05

bypass_paths.path: Write, delete, rename, directory listing or search through the broker
bypass_paths.evidence: Only route R1 exists and its mapping binds method, file id and read access mode (profile.md section 2); fixture FILES-06

bypass_paths.path: Remote access to the files over SMB from another host, with delegation and share-level permissions
bypass_paths.evidence: SMB stub profile smb.md: not claimed; excluded in unsupported_forms

bypass_paths.path: A Unix file broker or any other non-Windows file system adapter
bypass_paths.evidence: Unix stub profile unix.md: not claimed; excluded in unsupported_forms

unsupported_forms: Remote SMB delegation and share-level permission controls: the claim is a broker-local open of a local NTFS file under impersonation at the local impersonation level; the SMB stub profile (smb.md) is not claimed
Unix behavior: no Unix identity, permission, ACL or path semantics are claimed; the Unix stub profile (unix.md) is not claimed
Immediate revocation of an open handle: a handle keeps the access granted at open until the task ends, the deadline passes or the broker closes it; a revocation reaches only later opens
Broker-account fallback: the broker never opens a file under its own service identity, whether impersonation is unavailable, fails, or would produce a different executor
Any route other than GET /files/{file_id}/content, including every write, delete, rename, directory listing and search
Directories, reparse points of any kind (symbolic links, junctions, mount points, placeholders), and files whose data is not immediately available: they are rejected after open
Non-NTFS volumes, network paths and device namespaces: only fully qualified local NTFS paths registered by an administrator are served

Identity acquired by any means other than a completed Negotiate exchange: an OpenID Connect sign-in alone does not establish a Windows file-access token, and password-based, LsaLogonUser and service-for-user (S4U) acquisition are not implemented
Group requirements beyond comparing token group SIDs under a configured rule: no nested-group or SID-history semantics are claimed, and group lists are optional to this integration
Enforced purpose or data-use restrictions: execution-control-v1 is not claimed, so any such restriction is labeled attested-only and no egress or output control is claimed (draft section 17.4)

freshness.source: Enrollment registry (agent and key binding status)
Windows security context of the completed Negotiate exchange (principal SID and token group SIDs)
Native file open under impersonation (effective right to open the file)

membership_sources.source: Windows security context of the completed Negotiate exchange (principal SID and token group SIDs)

residual_limits: Post-read: file contents already returned to the agent are not recalled by a later revocation; execution-control-v1 is not claimed, so any purpose or data-use restriction is attested-only and no egress or output control is claimed (draft sections 17.4 and 18); disclosed here with no bound

Revocation propagation: a change to the enrollment registry, the delegation and task registry or the hold store reaches the broker at the next evaluation within each source's own consistency (status bound 0); a change to group membership reaches the broker only through a new Negotiate exchange and is bounded by the context age of 300 seconds plus an upstream lag that is not established; an operation already executed is not undone by revoking its receipt

Open handle: a handle already open keeps the access granted at open until the task ends, the deadline passes or the broker closes it; whether a later ACL or group change affects an open handle is an open item, and the profile claims no revocation of an open handle

Token snapshot: the principal and group SIDs are a snapshot taken when the context was established and no later check of account state takes place inside the context; the age of the directory data inside a new token (for example from a cached Kerberos service ticket) is not established and needs a domain controller to probe
Impersonation level: the broker obtains the local impersonation level only, so no remote resource is reached under the user's rights

Executor evidence: the immutable native record that names the actual executor identity for execution and authorization reports has no established native source; until one is named, the broker's own audit record is the evidence reference and its qualification is an open item
Path and object binding: any event that gives a registered file a new file identifier, or changes its final path, makes the broker refuse the file until an administrator registers it again
